The test image shows the underside of a leaf with:
- Small reddish-brown dots scattered across the surface
- White/cream cottony or powdery raised patches
- Visible leaf venation with some yellowing around veins

Top candidates: **Soybean_rust** (pustules on leaf underside) and **Downy_mildew** (white fuzzy growth on leaf underside). Let me view reference images.

**Analysis:**

- **Test image**: Underside of a soybean leaf with scattered reddish-brown dots and white/cream cottony raised pustule clusters distributed across the leaf surface. Leaf veins visible with some yellowing.

- **Soybean rust reference**: Top-right close-up shows tan-brown uredinia (rust pustules) on the leaf underside — pattern of scattered raised pustules matches the reddish dots in the test image. The white cottony material represents freshly erupted urediniospore masses.

- **Downy mildew**: Would show more uniform gray/white fuzzy coating without the discrete reddish pustule dots.

- **Bacterial_Pustule**: Shows more scattered small reddish-brown spots without the distinct white cottony raised clusters seen in the test image.

The test image is most consistent with **Soybean rust** — the combination of reddish-brown uredinia (mature pustules) and white spore masses on the leaf underside is the hallmark of this disease.
